item.title: In bid for transparency, Michigan swing county posts ballots online
item.description: Macomb County says its decision to make all ballots available online will increase transparency. Some worry about protecting secret ballots.

item.title: Michigan would regulate police license plate cameras under bipartisan bill
item.description: Michigan municipalities are increasingly turning to license plate readers as a public safety tool despite public outcry over privacy and data sharing concerns. Some lawmakers are pitching statewide oversight, but local law enforcement agencies are worried too much regulation could make the readers less effective for solving crimes.

item.title: Michigan sues prediction market Kalshi, alleging illegal sports betting
item.description: Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel has sued KalshiEx LLC, arguing the company is operating an unlicensed sports betting platform through its prediction market contracts.

item.title: Lots of tax cut promises, few specifics, from GOP gov hopefuls at forum
item.description: Four of six Republican governor candidates shared plenty of common ground during a Saginaw County forum, agreeing to slash taxes and government. They offered fewer answers about replacing lost revenue.

item.title: Michigan lags US in outdoor economy growth, report says
item.description: The US Bureau of Economic Analysis has released its latest outdoor recreation economic statistics. The outdoor industry’s contribution to Michigan’s economy grew in 2024 over the previous year, but at a slower rate than most other states.

item.title: Bridge Michigan News Quiz, March 6: We love winners
item.description: Following the news? Answer these questions about the week that was in Michigan.

item.title: Opinion | Massive national forest project needs a closer look at impacts, alternatives
item.description: The Forest Service must take a more careful look at the project’s impact on the adjacent Sturgeon River Gorge Wilderness, surrounding state and private lands, and the long-term health of the Ottawa National Forest.

item.title: Michigan town keeps zoning blocking trustee’s gravel mine
item.description: A northern Michigan township official wanted to end zoning, which would help him build a gravel mine. The township board just said no.

item.title: Michigan falls behind in race to save disappearing farmland
item.description: Thousands of farms and hundreds of thousands of acres of farmland have been lost to development and other economic pressures in recent years. Michigan does less than most to stem the tide.

item.title: Tech group: Michigan will be sued over efforts to restrain social media
item.description: A major tech group suggests Michigan would be sued if it tries to regulate minors’ access to social media. State lawmakers are undeterred.
